question: Mr. Saxena bought some pens at the rate of ₹150 per dozen. He sold them for 15 each. What is his profit/loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of **12 pens** (1 dozen) = ₹150.

Selling Price (SP) of **12 pens** = 12 × 15 = ₹180.

Profit = 180 − 150 = ₹30.

Profit % = (30 ÷ 150) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**
CP of 12 pens = ₹150 | SP of 1 pen = ₹15
**Formulas:**
Profit = SP − CP | Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acc21bbabec90ab3db2db49b9a70f8129a69e5e06263cf09fbcc7b25cef06f25.png] 
⇒ Calculate **CP of one pen** = 150 ÷ 12 = ₹12.5
⇒ **Selling Price** of one pen = ₹15
⇒ **Profit per pen** = 15 − 12.5 = ₹2.5
⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (2.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100
⇒ Profit Percentage = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conversion of Units

Always ensure both **Cost Price** and **Selling Price** are calculated for the same quantity (e.g., per item or per dozen) before finding profit or loss.

Profit/Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise in the question.
